comment: The table of the lexer in fort, src/fort/lexer.ft. Its rows hold the
rule that a source file is UTF-8 text (D2.1): each bound of a
well-formed sequence in utf8_len, and each of the five places that ask
it (a comment, a string literal, a char literal, the byte after a
backslash and the start of a token). 2 more rows hold the skip of a byte
order mark at the start (D2.1) and the limit of 20 diagnostics for a
file (D14.2). A row name gives the decision and the condition. The
stages are targeted: the lexer_ module suites of test/fort, then the
lexical areas of the language corpus and the one module test of the
rule. The table runs on a darwin host with --runner 'bash -c';
The md5 guard reads the product compiler that the build links.

stages.name: the lexer suites
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --root test/fort --fort build/Darwin/debug/fort --std-dir build/Darwin/debug/std --cc /opt/homebrew/bin/clang --target arm64-apple-macosx11.0.0 --opt /opt/homebrew/bin/opt --verify-ir -j 10 lexer_

stages.name: the lexical corpus
stages.command: python3 test/lang/run_tests.py --fort build/Darwin/debug/fort --std-dir build/Darwin/debug/std --cc /opt/homebrew/bin/clang --target arm64-apple-macosx11.0.0 --opt /opt/homebrew/bin/opt --verify-ir -j 10 --xfail test/lang/xfail.txt fail/lexical/ run/lexical/ fail/modules/035_

mutations.what: a continuation byte and the bytes 0xC0 and 0xC1 start a sequence of 2 bytes
the bytes 0xF5 to 0xFF start a sequence of 4 bytes
the byte 0xC1 starts a sequence, so an overlong form of 2 bytes is text
the byte 0xF4 starts no sequence, so U+100000 is no text
the byte 0xF0 starts a sequence of 3 bytes
the byte 0xE0 starts a sequence of 2 bytes
an overlong form of 3 bytes is text
the sequence 0xE0 0xA0 0x80, which is U+0800, is no text
a surrogate is text
the sequence 0xED 0x9F 0xBF, which is U+D7FF, is no text
the byte 0xEE and not the byte 0xED takes the short range
an overlong form of 4 bytes is text
the sequence 0xF0 0x90 0x80 0x80, which is U+10000, is no text
a code point above U+10FFFF is text
the sequence 0xF4 0x8F 0xBF 0xBF, which is U+10FFFF, is no text
an ASCII byte or the end of the file is a second byte
a byte above the range is a second byte
an ASCII byte or the end of the file is a third or a fourth byte
a byte above 0xBF is a third or a fourth byte
the byte 0x7F is a continuation byte
the byte 0xC0 is a continuation byte
the last byte of a sequence of 3 or 4 bytes is not read
a comment and a string literal take each byte, as before the rule
a comment takes each byte
a comment steps over the first byte of a sequence only

mutations.old:
puts each byte into the value (D3.7).
            u64 mut left = text_len(lx);
mutations.new:
puts each byte into the value (D3.7).
            u64 mut left = 1;
mutations.what: a string literal takes each byte
a string literal steps over the first byte of a sequence only

mutations.new: return fail_text(lx, here(lx), "non-ASCII byte in char literal; use a string");
mutations.what: a char literal gives its old error for bytes that are no UTF-8 text
the byte after a backslash gives the error of an unknown escape
a byte in code gives its old error for bytes that are no UTF-8 text

mutations.old:
msg_str(lx, "invalid UTF-8 sequence at byte ");
    msg_hex_byte(lx, peek(lx));
mutations.new:
msg_str(lx, "invalid UTF-8 sequence at byte ");
    msg_hex_byte(lx, peek_at(lx, 1));
mutations.what: the message names the second byte of the sequence
a byte order mark at the start is not skipped
the lexer reports past the limit of 20 diagnostics
